The statement signals a dovish pause: the FOMC holds rates and emphasizes “patience” amid slower activity and muted inflation pressures. This is consistent with estimated, forward-looking policy rules and interest-rate smoothing (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), the use of forward guidance to manage expectations (Svensson and Woodford), and concern that adverse global/financial shocks can be amplified via financial frictions (Bernanke–Gertler–Gilchrist). Low market-based inflation compensation suggests inflation expectations remain subdued, aligning with New Keynesian emphasis on expectations in the Phillips curve; patience helps re-anchor them near the symmetric 2% objective. Operationally, maintaining IOR at 2.40% reflects the modern floor system (Goodfriend, 2002). Net tone: slightly positive for risk assets and duration, more dovish than neutral but tempered by acknowledged growth slowing.
